name: Christoph Clement
headline: ML Engineer in AI Drug Discovery | PhD Biomedical Engineering | Applied AI Systems for Scientific & Clinical Workflows | CDTM
summary:
I am a Machine Learning Engineer at Khumbu, an AI drug discovery startup in Munich, where I build and scale applied AI systems for small-molecule drug discovery, with an initial focus on diabetes.
I recently completed a Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering at the University of Bern, focused on biomedical AI and medical imaging applications in nuclear medicine, and spent time as a visiting researcher at Harvard Medical School working on PET/CT foundation models.
I am especially interested in building AI systems that are technically strong, scientifically grounded, and useful in practice. Alongside my research and engineering work, I bring experience in customer-facing data science from Celonis, interdisciplinary product thinking from CDTM, and practical machine-learning experimentation through Kaggle.

company.name: Khumbu
company.tagline: Building the World Model for Molecular Biology.
company.description:
Khumbu is building the World Model for Molecular Biology. A fundamentally new AI, grounded in physics, that understands and simulates the molecular world. To transform how humanity discovers medicine.

Almost every drug discovery project ultimately fails in humans. Not because of bad science, but because we lack a proper model of what truly happens in biological systems.

Our AI learns the rules of the molecular world from first principles. Grounded in quantum mechanics and electromagnetism, it spans from atoms to proteins to biological systems. It generalizes where other approaches cannot, because the laws of physics are universal.  

And it already delivers real impact today.
